Rashi on Zevachim 10a:18:1.hebrew: שכן דמה למעלה: מחוט הסיקרא, דתנן במסכת מידות (פרק ג' משנה א') חוט הסיקרא חוגרת באמצע להבדיל בין דמים עליונים לדמים התחתונים. ויליף לקמן (זבחים דף נג:) מן והיתה הרשת עד חצי המזבח, התורה נתנה מחיצה להבדיל, וחטאת בהמה נעשית למעלה, דכתיב בה (ויקרא ד׳:) על קרנות, וכן עולת העוף (כדלקמן זבחים דף סד:). ושאר זבחים, שלא פירש בהן, נעשין למטה, דכתיב בהו מזבח ולא כתיב בהו קרנות, וכוליה מזבח ליכא למימר דהוה מקומן, שהרי תורה נתנה מחיצה: מחוט הסיקרא: זה חוט אדום החוגר את המזבח באמצעו להבדיל בין דמים העליונים לדמים התחתונים.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:19:1.hebrew: פסח יוכיח: שדמו למטה, כדאמרינן במתניתין, ועל זה פריך במתניתין דמה לפסח שכן זמנו קבוע:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:20:1.hebrew: מה לפסח: שכן זמנו קבוע לאשם דלית ליה זמן קבוע:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:21:1.hebrew: חטאת תוכיח: דלית ליה זמן קבוע ופסולה שלא לשמה ודמה למעלה:

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:10:1.hebrew: שאם נכנס דמה לפנים פסול - פירכא היא. וה"ק: ולימא ליה, מה לחטאת החיצונה שכן אם נכנס דמה לפנים פסולה, דכתיב (ויקרא ו׳:כ״ג) וכל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה כו', תאמר באשם דלא מיפסיל בהכי:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:10:1.english: For if its blood entered inside, it is disqualified - This is a refutation. And this is what [the Gemara] is saying: And [Rabbi Yehoshua] could have said to him: What [can be said] of the external sin offering, for if its blood entered inside, it is disqualified, as it is written (Leviticus 6:23): "And any sin offering, of whose blood is brought…" — will you say [the same] of a guilt offering, which is not disqualified by this?

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:11:1.hebrew: אית ליה לרבי אליעזר אף באשם - דם שנכנס דמו לפנים פסול, כדאיתא לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:11:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds "also [with regard to] a guilt offering" - That [a guilt offering] whose blood was brought inside is disqualified, as will be discussed later in this passage.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:11:2.hebrew: ולימא ליה - ר' יהושע: מה לחטאה, שכן מכפרת על חייבי כריתות:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:11:2.english: And let Rabbi Yehoshua say to him - What [proof is there] from a sin offering, since it atones for those liable to karet?

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:13:1.hebrew: מחטאת דשמיעת קול - יליף רבי אליעזר, דאינה באה על כרת:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:13:1.english: From the sin offering of hearing the voice - Rabbi Eliezer derives [the law] from it, because it does not come for [a transgression punishable by] karet.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:18:1.english: And why should Rabbi Eliezer not say to him: A guilt offering's blood is also sprinkled above the red line? Because Rabbi Eliezer equates a guilt offering to a sin offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:1:1.hebrew: חוזרני חלילה - ולא יקום הדין. ולקמן פריך: וניהדר דינא, וניתי ״במה הצד״:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:1:1.english: I return, around [again] - And the legal conclusion will not stand. And later [the Gemara] asks: But let the argument return, and let us come [to derive the law] through the "what is the common element" [argument]:

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:2:1.hebrew: נאמר בה היא בשחיטה - בחטאת שעיר נשיא:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:2:1.english: “It” is stated concerning it, in slaughter - [This refers to] the goat [sin offering] of the prince.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:32:1.hebrew: כל דמים: החיצונים שנכנסו להיכל לכפר — פסולין. ואף על גב דלא כתיב אלא 'וכל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה וגו'', מרבה רבי עקיבא קדשי קדשים וקדשים קלים מריבויא ד'כל' ו'כל' לקמן ב'כל הזבחים שנתערבו' (זבחים דף פב.):
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:32:1.english: All blood: This is referring to the external blood that entered the Sanctuary to atone, which is disqualified. This is so even though the verse only states: “And any sin offering, any of whose blood is brought, etc.” Rabbi Akiva includes Most Holy Offerings and Lesser Holy Offerings by expounding the superfluous words “kol” and “kol” (all) in the verse cited later in the chapter “In all mixed offerings” (Zevachim 82a).

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:5:1.hebrew: הרי הוא אומר כו' - ואין משיבין על ההיקש. ולקמן בסוף שמעתא מפרש טעמייהו דרבנן, דסמכי אהיקשא אחרינא, והך היקשא דרשינן למילתא אחריתי:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:5:1.english: Behold, it says, etc. - One does not refute a juxtaposition [with a counter-argument]. And below, at the end of the discussion, [the Gemara] explains the reasoning of the Rabbis: that they rely on a different juxtaposition, and this juxtaposition we expound for another matter.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:6:1.hebrew: תיתי במה הצד - דפסח וחטאת נאכלין (ליום ולילה), אף אני אביא אשם:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:6:1.english: Let it come by [the argument of] "what is the common element" - For the Paschal offering and the sin offering are [both] eaten (for a day and a night); so too I will bring the guilt offering [under the same law].

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:7:1.hebrew: צד כרת - חטאת באה על שגגת כרת, ופסח חייבים עליו כרת, והוא דווקא טהור שלא היה בדרך רחוקה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:7:1.english: An element of karet - A sin offering comes for an unintentional transgression [punishable by] karet, and one is liable to karet for [neglecting] the Paschal offering, [when one is] ritually pure and was not on a distant journey.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:8:1.english: Whose blood enters the innermost sanctum - For example, on Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Zevachim 10b:9:1.hebrew: בחטאות החיצונות קאמרינן - במתני' דפסולה. ואע"ג דלא עיילי לפנים, ומינייהו יליף ר' אליעזר:
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:9:1.english: We are speaking of the external sin offerings - in the Mishnah, where [the offering] is disqualified. And even though their blood does not enter inside, Rabbi Eliezer derives [the law] from them.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 10b:18.english: And in this, Rabbi Eliezer also agrees, for only Rabbi Akiva holds that all offerings whose blood entered the inner sanctuary are disqualified.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 10b:7.english: For a sin offering is brought (regularly) for a negative commandment that carries the penalty of karet, and a Paschal offering has an aspect of karet, as anyone who intentionally fails to bring it is liable to receive karet. And Tosafot write that one could also argue another reason for distinction: that the Paschal offering and the sin offering have an aspect of a communal offering, which is not the case with a guilt offering. And Tosafot ask: What about a provisional guilt offering (asham talui), which is brought for a doubtful transgression that carries the penalty of karet? And they answer that a provisional guilt offering does not atone, but rather serves to protect until it becomes known whether a sin was actually committed.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 10b:18.english: ב We continue to discuss that same baraita. The Master said: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: No, if you said this with regard to a sin offering, whose blood is indeed presented above the red line. And they ask: Let Rabbi Eliezer say to him: According to his view, a guilt offering's blood is also above the red line, since he equates the laws of a sin offering and a guilt offering!

Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:13:1.hebrew: מחטאת דשמיעת הקול - וליכא למיפרך: מה לשם חטאת, שכן כרת! דחדא מחדא לא פרכינן כל דהו:
Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:13:1.english: From the sin offering for hearing the voice - And one cannot refute [the derivation by saying]: What is true of the sin offering there [is because] it involves karet! For we do not refute [a derivation of] one from one in just any manner.

Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:18:1.hebrew: לימא ליה רבי אליעזר אשם נמי דמו למעלה - תימה, הלא במסקנא דשמעתא (דף יא א) קאמר רבא: אשם דמו למעלה לא מצית אמרת, אלא דמו למטה. וצ"ל דבתחילה לא היה אביי שואל אלא רבא שואל ומשני: חטאת העוף תוכיח וכדומה לזה. וכיון דחזר הדין קאמר: דליתי בהצד השוה שבהן, ופריך: מה להצד השוה שבהן שכן כרת? וכיון דאיכא פירכא ליתי בהיקשא, והוא דלא חשיב פירכא. ד"א: דשמעתין דלכתחילה קדשי קדשים דמן למעלה וקדשים קלים דמן למטה, ורבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע לא פליגי אלא לענין פסול שלא לשמן, ודמו למעלה הואיל ורבי אליעזר מקיש אשם לחטאת.

Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:4:1.hebrew: חטאת נאמר בה היא - בכמה מקומות משמע דמדכתיב "היא" נפקא לן עכובא. ותימה, דלעיל נפקא לן מקראי אחרינא! ולעיל (זבחים דף ה:) פירשתי:
Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:4:1.english: With regard to a sin offering, "it" is stated concerning it - In several places it is implied that from the fact that "it" is written, we derive that [the matter is] indispensable. And this is surprising, for earlier we derived it from other verses! And earlier (Zevachim 5b) I explained [this]:

Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:5:1.hebrew: הרי הוא אומר כחטאת כאשם - באשם מצורע כתיב. והוה מצי למילף אשם מחטאת בגזירה שוה דעון עון מחטאת דשמיעת קול, דהא למותרת נדבה גמירי, ואין ג"ש למחצה, כדאמר בריש מנחות (דף ד). אלא אי לאו היקשא הוה ממעט אשם מאותה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 10b:5:1.english: “It says: ‘As is the sin offering, so is the guilt offering’” - This is written regarding the guilt offering of the leper. And [Rabbi Eliezer] could have derived [the law of] the guilt offering from a sin offering through a verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) of “sin” and “sin,” from the sin offering for [violating an oath of] hearing a voice, since this [rule] is learned for the leftover of a voluntary offering, and there is no partial verbal analogy, as stated at the beginning of Menachot (4a). But were it not for the juxtaposition, he would have excluded the guilt offering from that [rule].

Zevachim 10a:17.english: The mishna teaches: Rabbi Eliezer says: The guilt offering, too, is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake. With regard to this [matter of the guilt offering] it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer said: A sin offering is brought for committing a transgression and a guilt offering is brought for committing a transgression. Just as a sin offering sacrificed not for its sake is unfit, so too, a guilt offering sacrificed not for its sake is unfit.

Zevachim 10a:18.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: The inference is not valid. If you say this with regard to a sin offering, whose blood is sprinkled above the red line that encircles the altar, should you necessarily say the same with regard to a guilt offering, whose blood is sprinkled below that line, like most animal offerings?

Zevachim 10a:19.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua: A Paschal offering can prove the point, as its blood is sprinkled below the red line (on the lower half of the altar), and nevertheless, if one slaughtered it not for its sake it is unfit.

Zevachim 10a:20.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: What is notable about a Paschal offering? It is notable in that its designated time is fixed. A guilt offering does not have a fixed time.

Zevachim 10a:21.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua: A sin offering can prove the point, as it does not have a fixed time, and nevertheless, it is disqualified if sacrificed not for its sake.

Zevachim 10a:22.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: I return to my previous claim that a sin offering is unique since its blood is sprinkled above the red line.

Zevachim 10b:18.english: The Master says: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: Your comparison is not valid. If you say this with regard to a sin offering, whose blood is sprinkled above the red line, should you necessarily say the same with regard to a guilt offering, whose blood is sprinkled below that line? The Gemara challenges: Let Rabbi Eliezer say to him: The blood of a guilt offering is also sprinkled above the red line, since Rabbi Eliezer holds that the halakhot of a guilt offering and a sin offering are parallel.
